catalog_quote: [p.216, 8.10] All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: púnuq [pú:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *púnuq and punúq [punúq] full < PBS *punúq. [p.218, 8.10.2] (1) CANONICAL FORM. In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form: all dialects sínsiŋ ring < PBS *sínsiŋ, all dialects búkbuk weevil < PBS *búkbuk. Regardless of the accent on the base form, if morphophonemic changes produce a form with a CVC-penult, the penult is stressed. Thus, Akl tułón to swallow + -a passive imperative → túnl-a swallow (it)!, Kin, Pan, Blk taqú- to give + -i local imperative → táwq-i give (it)!, Ceb punúq full + -a → púnq-a fill (it)! new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (352 pp., sealang PL-C44 scan with scanned text layer.). I re-extracted the cited pages with extracted text and read the surrounding sections. (1) pdf p.240 = p.216, sec. 8.10 'Proto Bisayan Accent': 'All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: punuq [pu:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *punuq and punuq [punuq] full < PBS *punuq' -- present; the reader's quote drops Zorc's acute accent marks and italics, otherwise verbatim. Same page also says inherited length 'is never found on the ultima, and in most Bs dialects (except Mas, Sor, N-S, S-L, War) is rest…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is contrastive (lexical) between penult and ultima in all surveyed Bisayan varieties, Camotes/Porohanon included; an accented open penult is realized with a long vowel; a closed (CVC) penult always takes the stress, including CVC penults created by affixation/syncope; accent is also manipulated morphologically by affix classes (sec. 4.2).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress; antepenultimate length is stated to be lost in Bisayan outside the Waray group (10.2.3 p.244).
new_statements.exceptions: Loss of contrastive accent only in some Kuyonon (Cuyo) and Jolo Tausug dialects; Camotes is not among the exceptions. Sentence stress can be overridden by intonation patterns (p.51).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonemic accent (length+stress) established by minimal pairs in citation forms; Zorc separately notes clause-level stress/intonation can shift stress while length remains (3.1.3 p.51). Statement is pan-Bisayan ('all dialects'), not a Camotes-specific paragraph; Zorc's Camotes data came from Wolff's notes (Table 2 data-source column 'Wolff').
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc 1977 treats the variety as 'Camotes Is. dialect, Porohanon' (abbrev. Cam; local name puruhanun), Peripheral Central Bisayan, = Glottolog poro1253 / ISO prh. Zorc's Camotes data are credited to Wolff (Table 2 data-source column), and the accent statements quoted are pan-Bisayan generalizations ('all Bs speech varieties', 'all dialects') that include Cam rather than a Camotes-specific paragraph. Santiago's 2018/2024 work describes the Poro municipality variety specifically.

sources.note: Pan-Bisayan statements that include Cam: all Bs speech varieties except some Kuy and Tsg dialects retain phonemic (contrastive) accent, penult vs ultima, minimal pair punuq 'tree trunk' vs punuq 'full' 'found in all dialects' (8.10 p.216); accented open penult has a long vowel (3.1.3 p.50); in all Bs dialects studied a closed penult is stressed, incl. CVC penults created by morphophonemics (8.10.2 p.218; 10.2.1 p.243); stress at sentence level interacts with intonation (p.51). Only Cam-specific phonology note is segmental (/z/ for general Bs /y/, p.49); no Cam-specific accent remark.
